newsitem.title: SPAIN: Austrian Economy Minister sees more flexible EMU.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Economy Minister sees more flexible EMU.

text.p: Austrian Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner said on Tuesday he sees a more flexible European economic and monetary Union (EMU) after the Socialist win at the French election this past Sunday.
"After the French vote we expect more flexibility in the meeting of convergence criteria," he told reporters during an official visit of Madrid.
He also said he preferred Italy being in the first EMU wave.
In Farnleitner's opinion, the change in the power in France would not mean a change in the euro project, although he expects social themes would play a more important role from now on.
"(The change of government in France) does not mean a long delay to European development, but in coming weeks we'll discuss more about joblessness," he said.
The Austrian Economy Minister said he favoured having Italy among the EMU's founder countries.
"For our competitiveness the euro is very important and we prefer Italy to be a member of the first group," he said.
Franleitner made his remarks in Spanish.
